sections.reason: Title block, Abstract, Status of This Memo, Copyright Notice and Table of Contents. Its one site is the IETF Trust Legal Provisions paragraph, excluded below.

Introduction. Indicative history of the MRT format, the projects that extended it, and the note that codes 0 through 10 are deprecated and documented in Appendix B. Its closing paragraph states the byte order, "Fields which contain multi-octet numeric values are encoded in network octet order from most significant octet to least significant octet", with no modal verb at all, so the site scan sees nothing to classify. The summary reads that sentence as a gated obligation, which is the unsourced id below.
Specification of Requirements. The RFC 2119 key-words paragraph. It binds no writer or reader and the derivation excludes it from the site inventory.

MRT Common Header. Field definitions for Timestamp, Type, Subtype, Length and Message, all indicative, plus the note that a post-2038 implementation will need an alternate epoch whose mechanism is out of scope. No modal verb in any case appears, so the prose scan derives no site. The field widths are carried by the Wire Formats table of rfc/short/rfc6396.md.
Extended Timestamp MRT Header. Defines the Microsecond Timestamp field, where it sits, and that it counts toward the Length. Indicative throughout, with no modal verb in any case.
MRT Types. The Type Code list (11 OSPFv2 through 49 OSPFv3_ET) and the sentence explaining the _ET suffix. A value table, not a directive.
OSPFv2 Type. Wire format of the OSPFv2 message field and what Remote IP Address, Local IP Address and OSPF Message Contents hold. Indicative; ze does not write this type.

TABLE_DUMP Type. Two capitalised MUST-level sites, mapped below to RFC6396-4.2-2 and RFC6396-4.2-1. Its remaining directives are advisory and carry no site: the RECOMMENDED to use TABLE_DUMP_V2 in new implementations, the MAY for decoding applications to support TABLE_DUMP, the MAY to use View Number to separate RIB views, the SHOULD to wrap the 16-bit Sequence Number, and the SHOULD to set the unused Status octet to 1. Those five are the unsourced ids below.
TABLE_DUMP_V2 Type. States what V2 adds over TABLE_DUMP and lists subtypes 1 through 6. A value table with no directive.

PEER_INDEX_TABLE Subtype. Three capitalised MUST-level sites, mapped below to RFC6396-4.3.1-3, -1 and -2. The rest is field definition: the Collector BGP ID, the Peer Count, and the Peer Entry fields Peer Type, Peer BGP ID, Peer IP Address and Peer AS, with the A and I bits of Peer Type and the rule that the peer index begins at 0. Every one of those is stated indicatively, so no site of this section obligates a WRITER about the VALUE it puts in a peer entry field, the Peer BGP ID included. They are carried by the Wire Formats table of rfc/short/rfc6396.md.
AFI/SAFI-Specific RIB Subtypes. Defines the RIB Entry Header and states that Prefix Length and Prefix follow the BGP NLRI encoding with irrelevant trailing bits. Indicative.

RIB_GENERIC Subtype. Defines the RIB_GENERIC Entry Header. Its one directive is the SHOULD to discard the remainder of an MRT record whose AFI and SAFI the implementation does not recognize, which is advisory and carries no site: the unsourced id below.

RIB Entries. One capitalised MUST-level site, mapped below to RFC6396-4.3.4-1. The MP_REACH_NLRI abbreviation is stated indicatively, "only the Next Hop Address Length and Next Hop Address fields are included. The Reserved field is omitted", with no modal verb, so the scan derives no site for it. The summary reads it as a gated obligation, which is the unsourced id below.
BGP4MP Type. Names the six BGP4MP subtypes and their codes. A value table with no directive.

BGP4MP_STATE_CHANGE Subtype. Wire format, the six FSM state values from RFC 4271 Section 8.2.2, and the AFI values. Its two directives are advisory and carry no site: the MAY to set an undefined Peer AS Number to zero and the MAY for an unknown or unsupported Interface Index to be zero. Those are the unsourced ids below.

BGP4MP_MESSAGE Subtype. Two capitalised MUST-level sites, mapped below to RFC6396-4.4.2-1 and RFC6396-4.4.2-2. The Interface Index MAY is a repeat of the section 4.4.1 statement and is carried by RFC6396-4.4.1-2, which section 4.4.1 lists as unsourced.
BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4 Subtype. One capitalised MUST-level site, mapped below to RFC6396-4.4.3-1. The rest states that the subtype is otherwise identical to BGP4MP_MESSAGE and shows the fields.
BGP4MP_STATE_CHANGE_AS4 Subtype. States that it is BGP4MP_STATE_CHANGE with 4-byte Peer and Local AS fields, and shows the format. Indicative.
BGP4MP_MESSAGE_LOCAL Subtype. States that the subtype marks a locally generated BGP message and that the Local fields name the collector while the Peer fields name the recipient. Indicative.
BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4_LOCAL Subtype. States that the fields are identical to BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4 and that the record marks a locally generated message. Indicative.
ISIS Type. States that the IS-IS PDU follows the MRT Common Header directly, that there is no type-specific header, and that the Subtype code is undefined. Indicative.
OSPFv3 Type. Wire format of the OSPFv3 message field, extending OSPFv2 with variable-length addresses. Indicative.

IANA Considerations. Registration guidance under BCP 26 for the Type Code and Subtype Code name spaces. Binds IANA and the authors of future MRT specifications, not an MRT writer or reader. Its one site is the BCP 26 policy-name sentence, excluded below.

Type Codes. The allocation policy for the Type Code registry: 0-64 reserved, new codes from 65, IETF Review to 511, Specification Required to 2047, First Come First Served to 64511, Experimental Use to 65534, and 65535 reserved. Site 5.1:1 carries the allocation floor and maps to RFC6396-5.1-1, which rfc/short/rfc6396.md declares; site 5.1:2 is a policy-name match the case-insensitive scan made and is excluded below.

Subtype Codes. States that Subtype definitions are specific to a Type Code and that Subtype assignments follow the rules of their Type Code. Its one site binds the author of a future MRT Subtype definition and is excluded below.
Defined Type Codes. The registry table of the twenty Type Codes this document defines, each pointing at the section that specifies it.
Defined BGP, BGP4PLUS, and BGP4PLUS_01 Subtype Codes. A registry table for the deprecated BGP Type's eight subtypes.
Defined TABLE_DUMP Subtype Codes. A registry table: AFI_IPv4 is 1 and AFI_IPv6 is 2.
Defined TABLE_DUMP_V2 Subtype Codes. A registry table: PEER_INDEX_TABLE 1 through RIB_GENERIC 6.
Defined BGP4MP and BGP4MP_ET Subtype Codes. A registry table for the six BGP4MP subtypes, and the closing note that BGP4MP_ET shares them.

Security Considerations. States that the MRT fields are descriptive and induce no behavior in the recipient application, that peer IP addresses, next hops and path attributes can be sensitive, and that an organization publishing MRT dumps beyond its domain should check with the peers whose information is included. That last direction binds the operator publishing an archive rather than the MRT writer, it carries no RFC 2119 keyword, and the summary declares no requirement for it.
References. The heading itself, with the two subsections below carrying the entries.
Normative References: IANA-AF, RFC 791, RFC 1195, RFC 2119, RFC 2328, RFC 2460, RFC 3629, RFC 4271, RFC 4760, RFC 5226, RFC 5340.
Informative References: GEOMRT, MRT_PROG_GUIDE, POSIX, RFC 4272.

MRT Encoding Examples. The appendix says so in its own first sentence, "This appendix, which is not normative, contains MRT encoding examples". It shows one BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4 record and one TABLE_DUMP_V2 pair in hexadecimal.
Deprecated MRT Types. Two indicative sentences: the appendix lists deprecated types, and they are documented for informational purposes. The subsections below carry what text there is.

Deprecated MRT Informational Types. Codes 0 through 4, which the section itself says are not known to be implemented. One capitalised MUST-level site, mapped below to RFC6396-B.1-1. Its one advisory directive, the SHOULD to set the unused Subtype field to 0, carries no site and is the unsourced id below.
NULL Type. One sentence: the NULL Type message causes no operation.
START Type. One sentence: the record indicates that a collector is about to begin generating MRT records.

DIE Type. One sentence, carrying the advisory SHOULD that a remote MRT repository stop accepting messages. It is advisory, so the scan derives no site; the summary declares it as the unsourced id below.
I_AM_DEAD Type. One sentence: the record indicates that a collector has shut down and stopped generating MRT records.
PEER_DOWN Type. States what the record was intended for and that the BGP state change types duplicate the function. Indicative.
Other Deprecated MRT Types. The code list 5 through 10: BGP, RIP, IDRP, RIPNG, BGP4PLUS and BGP4PLUS_01. A value table.
BGP Type. States that the Message field carries BGP routing information, that the content depends on the Subtype, and that the type and all its subtypes are deprecated by BGP4MP. Indicative.
BGP_NULL Subtype. One sentence: the subtype is unused and deprecated.
BGP_UPDATE Subtype. Wire format of the deprecated BGP_UPDATE record and its Peer AS, Peer IP, Local AS, Local IP and BGP UPDATE fields. Indicative.
BGP_PREF_UPDATE Subtype. States that the format was never fully specified and is not known to be implemented. Indicative.
BGP_STATE_CHANGE Subtype. Wire format of the deprecated state-change record and the note that the AS and IP fields are 2-byte and IPv4. Indicative.

BGP_SYNC Subtype. Describes a record whose use is unclear with no known implementations. Its one advisory statement, that the subtype should be ignored, carries no capitalised keyword site and is the unsourced id below.
BGP_OPEN Subtype. States that the record encodes a received BGP OPEN message in the BGP_UPDATE format. Indicative.
BGP_NOTIFY Subtype. States that the record encodes a received BGP NOTIFICATION message in the BGP_UPDATE format. Indicative.
BGP_KEEPALIVE Subtype. States that the record encodes a received BGP KEEPALIVE message in the BGP_UPDATE format. Indicative.

RIP Type. States that the Message field carries a RIP packet and that the type is deprecated. Its advisory statement that the unused Subtype field should be set to 0 covers this section and B.2.4, carries no capitalised keyword site, and is the unsourced id below.
IDRP Type. States that the type was intended to carry IDRP information, that the format was never fully specified, and that no implementation is known. Indicative.
RIPNG Type. States that the Message field carries a RIPng packet and that the type is deprecated. Its unused-Subtype statement is the one RFC6396-B.2.2-1 covers, listed as unsourced on section B.2.2.
BGP4PLUS and BGP4PLUS_01 Types. States that the two types encode BGP with multiprotocol extensions in early Zebra releases and are deprecated by BGP4MP. Indicative.
Deprecated BGP4MP Subtypes. Names subtypes 2 and 3, BGP4MP_ENTRY and BGP4MP_SNAPSHOT, as deprecated. A value table.
BGP4MP_ENTRY Subtype. Wire format of the deprecated RIB entry record, deprecated by TABLE_DUMP_V2. Indicative.
BGP4MP_SNAPSHOT Subtype. Describes a record pointing at an external dump file, with the note that it is not known to be implemented. Indicative.
Acknowledgements, and with it the unnumbered Authors' Addresses block, which carries no section number and so stays in this body under the heading derivation.

sites.quote: Code Components extracted from this document must include Simplified BSD License text as described in Section 4.e of the Trust Legal Provisions and are provided without warranty as described in the Simplified BSD License.
sites.reason: The IETF Trust Legal Provisions paragraph of the Copyright Notice, which the boilerplate filter does not strip because it names the Simplified BSD License rather than RFC 2119. Its "must" binds a person who extracts a code component from the document, and it states a licensing condition rather than a protocol obligation.

sites.quote: The TABLE_DUMP_V2 Type MUST be used in these situations.
sites.reason: The obligation to use TABLE_DUMP_V2 when the peer AS needs 4 bytes or the peer IP AFI differs from the prefix AFI, captured as RFC6396-4.2-2 at [MUST]. "These situations" is the preceding sentence, which names both.

sites.quote: The AS_PATH attribute MUST only consist of 2-byte AS numbers.
sites.reason: The 2-byte AS_PATH obligation on a TABLE_DUMP writer, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.2-1 at [MUST].

sites.quote: The RIB entry MRT records MUST immediately follow the PEER_INDEX_TABLE MRT record.
sites.reason: The ordering obligation that RIB entry records follow the PEER_INDEX_TABLE record immediately, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.3.1-3 at [MUST].

sites.quote: The View Name is OPTIONAL and, if not present, the View Name Length MUST be set to 0.
sites.reason: The obligation to write View Name Length 0 when no view name is present, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.3.1-1 at [MUST].

The UTF-8 obligation on the View Name encoding, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.3.1-2 at [MUST]. The derived quote runs on into the Figure 5 diagram because the sentence terminator is followed by the diagram's own digits, which the sentence splitter needs a capital, a quote or a bracket to cut at. The obligation is the leading sentence.

sites.quote: All AS numbers in the AS_PATH attribute MUST be encoded as 4-byte AS numbers.
sites.reason: The 4-byte AS_PATH obligation on a TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB entry, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.3.4-1 at [MUST].

sites.quote: The AS_PATH contained in these messages MUST only consist of 2-byte AS numbers.
sites.reason: The 2-byte AS_PATH obligation on a BGP4MP_MESSAGE record, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.4.2-1 at [MUST].

sites.quote: Only one BGP message SHALL be encoded in the BGP4MP_MESSAGE Subtype.
sites.reason: The one-message-per-record obligation, captured as RFC6396-4.4.2-2. The source states it at SHALL and the summary row reads [MUST]; RFC 2119 Section 1 makes the two synonymous and both gate.

sites.quote: The AS_PATH in these messages MUST only consist of 4-byte AS numbers.
sites.reason: The 4-byte AS_PATH obligation on a BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4 record, captured verbatim as RFC6396-4.4.3-1 at [MUST].

sites.quote: The following policies are used here with the meanings defined in BCP 26: "Specification Required", "IETF Consensus", "Experimental Use", "First Come First Served".
sites.reason: A sentence naming the four BCP 26 registration policies this document uses. The prose scan matches it on "Required" inside the policy name "Specification Required", which is a proper name quoted from BCP 26 and not a directive to anyone.

sites.quote: New Type Codes MUST be allocated starting at 65.
sites.reason: The allocation floor for new MRT Type Codes, captured verbatim as RFC6396-5.1-1 at [MUST]. It binds IANA and the summary records that in the row's own annotation; it is mapped rather than excluded because the summary declares the id, and a gated id the walk leaves unmapped is what the reverse arithmetic refuses.

sites.quote: Type Codes 512-2047 are assigned based on Specification Required.
sites.reason: A registry allocation statement: Type Codes 512 to 2047 are handed out under the BCP 26 "Specification Required" policy. The prose scan matches it on "Required" inside that policy name. The sentence is indicative and directs nobody.

sites.quote: New Subtype Code definitions must reference an existing Type Code to which the Subtype belongs.
sites.reason: The role is the author of a future MRT Subtype specification, and behind them the IANA registry that will refuse a Subtype naming no Type Code. Ze neither allocates MRT Subtype codes nor writes MRT specifications, so no MRT writer or reader in ze is bound by it. The role is a specification author and the IANA registry behind them, so no producer could act as it. Ze only WRITES records under codes already assigned: `asyncWriter.Write` (`internal/plugins/mrt/async_writer.go`).

sites.quote: The message string encoding MUST follow the UTF-8 transformation format [RFC3629].
sites.reason: The UTF-8 obligation on the optional diagnostic message string of the deprecated Informational Types, captured verbatim as RFC6396-B.1-1 at [MUST].

register-reason: Standards Track, with the RFC 2119 key-words paragraph at section 1.1. Eleven of the fifteen derived sites carry a capitalised MUST-level keyword, which is fewer than the thirteen gated rows rfc/short/rfc6396.md declares, so the derivation grades the source 'prose' and the sign-off claims exactly that grade. The four remaining sites come from the case-insensitive scan and are excluded below. The gap of two between eleven keyword sites and thirteen gated rows is accounted for exactly: RFC6396-1-1 and RFC6396-4.3.4-2 are both read from indicative prose that carries no modal verb, and each is listed as an unsourced id on the section it was read from.
